title: Unwrap or Default
story: A visitor lands on your website. Your code looks for their username — but they might be anonymous. Instead of crashing, you show 'Guest' as a friendly fallback. How?
why: .unwrap_or(default) provides a clean one-liner to extract a value from an Option or fall back to a safe default — no match boilerplate needed.
analogy: .unwrap_or is like having a backup plan — "I'll use my umbrella, but if I can't find it, I'll grab the spare one by the door."
try_it: Try different defaults: unwrap to 0, unwrap to an empty string "", unwrap to "Unknown". What happens when you call .unwrap_or on a Some value? Does it ever use the default?
tips: .unwrap_or() works on any Option[T] — the default must be the same type as T
Use .unwrap_or when you have a sensible fallback — it's cleaner than a full match
The default value is NOT computed if the Option is Some — it's only used for None
common_mistakes: Providing a default of the wrong type — `option_int.unwrap_or("hello")` won't compile
Using .unwrap_or when the default is expensive to compute and the Some case is common — in that case, match lets you avoid computing it
Confusing .unwrap_or with .unwrap — .unwrap() crashes on None, .unwrap_or() safely provides a fallback
